hints: Remember what initiation means in a free radical mechanism, splitting one covalent bond homolytically to make two radicals from a stable molecule.
Compare the bonds in $\text{CH}_2\text{FCl}$, the $\text{C-Cl}$ bond is much weaker than $\text{C-H}$ and $\text{C-F}$, so it breaks most easily in UV light.
Look for the equation that breaks only that weakest bond to release a chlorine radical plus one carbon radical.
walkthrough:
**Recall what initiation must do**

Think of initiation as the starter step. One stable molecule absorbs UV energy and one bond splits evenly, with one electron going to each side.

General rule:
$$\text{X-Y} \xrightarrow{uv} \text{X}^{\bullet} + \text{Y}^{\bullet}$$

**Identify the bonds in chlorofluoromethane**

Our molecule is $\text{CH}_2\text{FCl}$. It contains $\text{C-H}$, $\text{C-F}$ and $\text{C-Cl}$ bonds.

Only one bond should break to give two radicals. Breaking two bonds at once is far too energy demanding for initiation.

**Pick the weakest bond**

Bond strength follows $\text{C-F} > \text{C-H} > \text{C-Cl}$. The $\text{C-Cl}$ bond is the longest and weakest, about $340 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ compared to about $410$ for $\text{C-H}$ and $467$ for $\text{C-F}$.

So UV light will selectively cause homolytic fission of $\text{C-Cl}$:
$$\text{CH}_2\text{FCl} \rightarrow {}^{\bullet}\text{CH}_2\text{F} + \text{Cl}^{\bullet}$$

**Link to ozone damage**

It is the $\text{Cl}^{\bullet}$ radical that goes on to catalyse the breakdown of ozone. That is why CFCs are dangerous, they are a source of $\text{Cl}^{\bullet}$ in the upper atmosphere.

options.A: This shows breaking of the C-F bond to give F dot. The C-F bond is very strong and does not break easily in initiation. Also, it is Cl dot, not F dot, that is the key ozone-destroying radical.
options.B: This shows homolytic fission of the weakest C-Cl bond to give Cl dot plus the ${}^{\bullet}\text{CH}_2\text{F}$ radical. This needs the least energy and correctly supplies the chlorine radical that damages ozone.
options.C: This shows breaking of a C-H bond to give H dot. The C-H bond is stronger than C-Cl, so it is much less likely to break first. H dot is not the chain carrier for ozone depletion.
options.D: This breaks two bonds at once to give Cl dot, F dot and a carbene (:CH2). Initiation breaks only one bond to make two radicals. Breaking two bonds needs far too much energy and does not give the correct radical pair.
